title: Somatic Symptom Disorder - DSM-5-TR Full Criteria and Evidence Base
content:
A. One or more somatic symptoms that are distressing or result in significant disruption of daily life.
B. Excessive thoughts, feelings, or behaviors related to the somatic symptoms or associated health concerns as manifested by at least one of the following:
1. Disproportionate and persistent thoughts about the seriousness of one's symptoms.
2. Persistently high level of anxiety about health or symptoms.
3. Excessive time and energy devoted to these symptoms or health concerns.
C. Although any one somatic symptom may not be continuously present, the state of being symptomatic is persistent (typically more than 6 months).

Specifiers:
- With predominant pain (formerly Pain Disorder): The somatic symptoms predominantly involve pain.
- Persistent: A persistent course is characterized by severe symptoms, marked impairment, and long duration (more than 6 months).
- Mild, Moderate, Severe (based on number of B criteria met and degree of impairment).

Differential Diagnosis: Illness Anxiety Disorder (preoccupation without prominent somatic symptoms), Conversion Disorder (Functional Neurological Symptom Disorder), Factitious Disorder, Malingering, Other Medical Conditions, Depressive Disorders, Anxiety Disorders, Body Dysmorphic Disorder, OCD (illness obsessions).

Common Comorbidities: MDD, GAD, Panic Disorder, PTSD, Personality Disorders (especially histrionic, borderline), Substance Use Disorders.

Research Evidence Base (2024-2026): APA recommends CBT as first-line (focus on reducing health anxiety, behavioral activation, cognitive restructuring of illness beliefs). Avoid unnecessary medical tests/reassurance-seeking. Collaborative care models in primary care reduce utilization by 30-50%. 2024 reviews emphasize "illness behavior" as target rather than symptom elimination. Voice research: Somatic patients often show high arousal + low valence during symptom description, with frequent sighing or throat-clearing; reassurance-seeking speech patterns detectable. Stepped-care approaches (self-help → guided CBT → specialist) effective.

Vocal/Behavioral State Vector (BSV) Relevance: Moderate-high Arousal (anxiety about symptoms), Low-moderate Valence (distress, frustration with medical system), moderate Dominance (help-seeking). Voice may convey physical discomfort (strained, breathy) even when no acute medical finding.
